title: feat(idd-doctor): warn when fully_autonomous_merge is unacknowledged
body:
# feat(idd-doctor): warn when fully_autonomous_merge is unacknowledged

## Background

Parent roadmap: #2286

Blocked by #2284

The warning text names the shipped distributed default from issue
`#2284`, so this check cannot start until that contract is on `main`.

After autonomous merge becomes an opt-in, adopters who already have
`mergePolicy: "fully_autonomous_merge"` in `.github/idd/config.json`
keep that recorded value, including cases that got there by accepting
the old default. They need a visible reminder that the profile is now
opt-in, without failing CI or forcing a re-confirm.

`idd-doctor` already exits `0` when the report has warnings and no
errors, so a warning-severity finding is informational.

**Revision note (superseding an earlier no-suppression design):** an
earlier draft of this issue had the warning fire unconditionally on
every `idd-doctor` run for as long as `fully_autonomous_merge` stayed
recorded, with no way to acknowledge it. That does not fit this
repository's own `idd-doctor` precedent: every other warning-level
finding (`claimTiming` config↔prose drift, `worktreeGuard.enabled`
without a wired hook, a CRLF-broken hook) is a *clearable* defect —
fix the underlying state and the finding disappears next run. An
unconditional nag has no clearing action short of abandoning the
deliberate choice, and `idd-doctor` runs on every push
(`pre-push-validate` in `.github/idd/config.json`) and on every pull
request (`.github/workflows/idd-doctor.yml`, `on: pull_request`) — so
a repository that knowingly keeps `fully_autonomous_merge` (this
source repository included; see `CLAUDE.md`'s
`fully_autonomous_merge` dogfooding-policy note) would see the same
unactionable warning on every single IDD loop iteration, forever. A
warning nobody can ever resolve trains readers to stop reading
`idd-doctor` warnings at all, which weakens the signal for every
other, genuinely actionable finding it reports. This revision keeps
the reminder for the case it actually targets — a value inherited
from the old fail-open default that nobody has affirmatively
reconsidered — while letting an operator who has knowingly opted in
silence it.

**Scope note on `mergePolicyAck` vs. the #2284 locked decision:** issue
`#2284`'s authoring hearing locked "`fully_autonomous_merge` remains a
valid explicit opt-in. Do not add a second schema flag" — that decision
is about not needing a second flag to represent the opt-in *itself*;
once `human_merge` ships as the default, the recorded `mergePolicy`
enum value alone is enough to grant F3 merge authority, and this issue
does not touch that. `mergePolicyAck` is a narrower, diagnostics-only
field: it never participates in F2.5/F3 merge-authority resolution,
never changes what an unrecorded or recorded `mergePolicy` value
authorizes, and only gates whether `idd-doctor` prints this one
reminder. Confirmed with the repository owner before drafting this
revision.

## Proposed change

Add an optional `mergePolicyAck` field to the policy schema
(`schemas/policy.schema.json`), typed as the same string enum as
`mergePolicy` (`fully_autonomous_merge` | `human_merge` |
`separate_merge_agent`). It records that the operator has explicitly
reconsidered and confirmed the current `mergePolicy` value.

In `src/scripts/idd-doctor.mts`, when `.github/idd/config.json` (or
the existing `idd-policy.json` candidate, if that is the file being
read) has `mergePolicy` equal to `fully_autonomous_merge` **and**
`mergePolicyAck` is absent or does not equal `"fully_autonomous_merge"`,
push a warning-severity finding that this profile is an explicit
opt-in, that the distributed default is `human_merge`, and how to
silence the reminder (set `mergePolicyAck: "fully_autonomous_merge"`
once the value is confirmed).

Do not fail the doctor exit code on this finding. Do not warn for
`human_merge`, `separate_merge_agent`, a missing config file, a
config whose `mergePolicy` key is absent, or a config whose
`mergePolicyAck` already equals the live `mergePolicy` value.
`mergePolicyAck` is intentionally scoped to the current value, not a
one-time boolean: if `mergePolicy` later changes and is changed back,
the stale ack (for the old value only) no longer matches and the
warning resumes until re-confirmed.

Update this repository's own `.github/idd/config.json` to add
`mergePolicyAck: "fully_autonomous_merge"` in the same change, so
this source repository's deliberate, documented dogfood choice
(`CLAUDE.md`) exercises the clearing path instead of nagging itself
on every push.

Cover the new finding in `tests/idd-doctor.test.mts`, including the
ack-present, ack-absent, ack-mismatched-value, and ack-for-a-different-
`mergePolicy` cases. Edit the TypeScript source, not the generated
`.mjs`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `idd-doctor` reports a warning (not an error) when the live
      config `mergePolicy` is `fully_autonomous_merge` and
      `mergePolicyAck` is absent or not equal to
      `"fully_autonomous_merge"`.
- [ ] The warning text states that `fully_autonomous_merge` is an
      opt-in, that the distributed default is `human_merge`, and how
      to acknowledge the value to silence the warning.
- [ ] No warning is emitted when `mergePolicyAck` equals
      `"fully_autonomous_merge"`.
- [ ] The process still exits `0` when that warning is the only
      finding.
- [ ] No warning is emitted for `human_merge`,
      `separate_merge_agent`, a missing config file, or a config
      without a `mergePolicy` key.
- [ ] `schemas/policy.schema.json` accepts an optional
      `mergePolicyAck` field with the same enum as `mergePolicy`, and
      a config with an unrelated/stale `mergePolicyAck` value still
      validates (it only affects the doctor warning, never schema
      validity).
- [ ] This repository's `.github/idd/config.json` records
      `mergePolicyAck: "fully_autonomous_merge"` so its own
      `idd-doctor` run stays warning-free for this finding.
- [ ] `tests/idd-doctor.test.mts` covers the warning and the
      non-warning cases above.
- [ ] `pnpm run lint:minimum` passes.

## Candidate files

- `src/scripts/idd-doctor.mts`
- `schemas/policy.schema.json`
- `.github/idd/config.json`
- `tests/idd-doctor.test.mts`
